{"number":1138,"title":"Label scheme PRs 1–2: decode every spelling, and the marked issue becomes the item","body":"#1119's review pass, **stages 1 and 2**, as two separate commits on one branch — this session may only push to its designated branch, so the plan's stacked-PR shape collapsed into one PR. Say the word and I will split stage 2 onto its own branch based on this one.

**PR 3 (the write-side flip) is deliberately not here**: the plan gates its merge on the fleet force that happens *after* 1–2 merge, so landing it beside them would jump that gate.

## Stage 1 — the read side + the stubs (commit `eef03a4`)

Additive on every member, in any order: **nothing writes a canonical status yet**.

- **One decode pass.** `work-item.mjs` gains the canonical vocabulary (`STATUS_*`, `ORIGIN_*`) and `statusOf` / `statusesOn` / `isParked` / `parkKindOf` / `originOf`. Every legacy spelling in DESIGN §4's table maps straight to today's, in one pass; a park whose kind cannot be decoded — an older engine's bare `needs-human`, a word a newer engine invents — reads as `failure`, the lane that holds the task's lane. No reader compares a label literally any more.
- **Transitions leave a status, not a label.** New `apply-status.mjs`: leaving a status clears *every* spelling of it, so an item filed as `task:ready` and picked up by an engine writing the canonical spelling cannot end up wearing two live statuses. The flip is then six constants changing. Side effect worth naming: a hand wake now clears the park's sub-label too, which it previously left standing.
- **The ensure-list carries the canonical labels already** — GitHub 422s an attempt to apply a label that does not exist, and the ensure pass reaches a member a converge before the flip does.
- **Both stubs, and the canon's own copies.** The executor triggers on `task:status:waiting-for-executor` *and* `task:ready` (and `task:urgent`) — a workflow's event trigger names label strings literally, so this is the one surface where both vocabularies must appear at once. Both workflows file their failure issues as `task:origin:github` + `task:status:needs-human-failure`, ensuring those labels first.

## Stage 2 — one-issue requests (commits `e2b5541`, `6e6529b`)

The shadow work item is gone. A person marks an ordinary issue `task:origin:ad-hoc`; adoption appends the machine block to **that issue's own body** and applies the first status; the lifecycle plays out where the person is already looking.

- **One lever.** Any status — live, parked or terminal — holds the mark until somebody clears it. No prior item to wait on, none to supersede; an impatient re-ask mid-run is structurally nothing.
- **Parameters ride the person's text**, not labels: `Task:`, `Model:`, `Automerge:`, beside `Blocked-by:` and `Not-before:`. Re-read at every adoption and honoured only for an author with push access, read from the collaborators-permission API — never the payload's association. An ungated ask still runs, at the defaults, and the adoption comment says so.
- **`Task: /` is new** — which task a mark asks for, defaulting to the built-in implementer. An id this repo does not carry is not adopted at all: the mark waits. Recorded as DESIGN §16.12, since §16 only sketched it.
- **Nothing closes somebody's issue.** A refusal's terminal status stands on the open issue — the run's verdict is not the issue's validity — and so does the approval park, which *is* the in-review state.
- **Identity without a title**: a marked issue's task comes from the worker path its machine block names (`taskIdFromPath`). That closed two holes — the janitor's stale-ready rule skipped every request run, and the dashboard rendered them as belonging to no task.
- **Legacy is read forever**: `claude-task` still marks (and adoption gives the issue today's origin), and a draining shadow item still writes back to the issue it names.

## Findings for the plan

- **The stubs are converge-delivered, not copied-once** — `convergeWiring` rewrites both workflow files from the vendored stubs whole. Execution step 1's contingency does not apply. The lag is that `.github/workflows/` lands as a PR somebody merges, so a member spends a window on the old copy — costing a label event, never work, since the hourly scheduler dispatch is the guaranteed delivery. That window is now a rehearsal shape.
- **`consumer-safe-change` watched only the scheduler stub.** The executor's is vendored just as verbatim and its trigger is exactly the surface a vocabulary change must carry members across, so the check (canon-local) now covers both.
- **Left out of stage 2, deliberately**: folding `add-packs` into the `Task:` field. It rewrites a cross-repo contract (the enforcer writes into members over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`), and its real failure mode needs a decision — a member whose mark label does not exist yet refuses the enforcer's write, and nothing runs, where the current dispatch-and-wake protocol is robust to that. Everything the fold needs on this side is now in place.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/queue/       the decode + apply-status; the machine block and the
                              request-side field parse; adoption rewritten to write
                              onto the marked issue; executor/converge identity and
                              the never-close rule; the built-in task and its doc
engine/scheduler/signals/     the request read accepts either mark
engine/scheduler/stubs/       both workflow stubs — the executor's dual trigger, and
.github/workflows/            the canon's own hand-maintained copies of the same two
packs/basics/                 the janitor's queue sweep decodes; do-later and
                              verify-in-production speak the mark and the body fields
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   item state, triage, parked counts and item membership
vendoring/rehearsal/          the old-workflows fixture gains the pre-#1119 executor
docs/tasks-dispatch/          DESIGN §16.12 — the `Task:` targeting field
.claudinite/local/packs/…     consumer-safe-change now watches both stubs
```

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2409 pass, 1 fail: `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails on `main` too in this sandbox (shallow clone; the test refuses to walk a partial history). `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking, 67 advisory — the same 67 as on `main`.

`engine-tests/scheduler/queue/vocabulary.test.mjs` (new) pins the decode table, park precedence, the mid-flip both-spellings case, the ensure-list, the stub triggers read from the real files, and the machinery reacting to canonical items — seen to fail with the source reverted. `request-mode.test.mjs` is rewritten to the one-issue model: S44 is now the one-lever guard (S49/S51 collapse into it), S47 covers the body's `Model:` and the author gate, and three new tests drive the executor end-to-end over a marked issue.

{"number":1163,"title":"Link PRs and issues where GitHub renders it","body":"GitHub's **Development** panel ("Successfully merging this pull request may close these issues") is the link between a PR and its issue that anyone browsing either one follows. It is filled by a closing keyword in the **PR body**; our lifecycle only asked for a reference in a *commit message*, which `task-lifecycle` checks but which leaves the panel reading "None yet".

Landed as prose, since no rung above it is available here: the check vocabulary scans the repo tree and branch commits, and a PR body is neither. Assurance for the prose rung — the corpus carries nothing on this today: the only `sub-issue` mentions are `verify-in-production`'s own step and two "log as a dated comment, **not** a sub-issue" rules, and nothing anywhere mentions the Development panel or closing keywords in a PR body.

- `packs/basics/RULES.md` — the task lifecycle gains step 3 (open the PR with `Closes #123` on its own line in the body; `Refs #123` links nothing there; a PR that must not close its issue gets the slice its own issue), and a new rule *Filing an issue that belongs under another* — attach it as a sub-issue rather than naming a number in prose.
- `packs/basics/skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md` — each chain link is a sub-issue of the tracking issue, and a phase PR closes **its link**, never the tracker: `Closes #` on a phase PR ends the whole migration on its first merge.

- `packs/basics/README.md` — the rule-index row for the new rule, and the recount of two rows whose blocks this edit changed.
- `packs/basics/pack.mjs` — version bump, so the change reaches members.

{"number":1195,"title":"Design pack-contributed dashboard metrics","body":"Adds `docs/dashboard-pack-metrics/DESIGN.md`: the contract by which any pack surfaces its own key figures on the dashboard's repo and fleet views.

The design in brief — **a pack contributes data, never code**:

- A pack carries one vendored descriptor, `packs//dashboard.json`, schema-validated, declaring its repo-page card (≤6 widgets), at most one compact per-member signal for the fleet view, and optionally one deployment-scope fleet card.
- Values come from either the pack's own `.claudinite/local/dashboard/.GENERATED.json` (written by the pack's own task, read at the head sha — free while `main` has not moved) or the one sanctioned live source, `latest-release` (one ETag'd read per repo, shared).
- Four widget kinds (`stat`, `event`, `window`, `list`), rendered only by the dashboard's own bounded renderers through `textContent`; `window` is the only shape for counts of happenings, per the no-vanity-total rule.
- Discovery costs zero probe reads (both views already hold the declaration and tree listing at the head sha); pack metrics sit at the commit-graph rung of the budget policy and are skipped first.
- Pack contributions never feed attention, ordering, or rollup tiles; every miss renders as a named absence; version skew is tolerated per member (descriptor and values come from the same tree at the same sha).

Alternatives (pack render code, HTML fragments, one shared metrics file, descriptor-in-values, contributing via the usage fold, free-form live sources) are in the doc with their drawbacks.

Closes #1194

{"number":1152,"title":"Label scheme PR 3: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119's plan — the write-side flip. #1138 has landed, so this is rebased onto `main` and its one commit is only the flip.

> ⚠️ **Do not merge before the gate.** The plan gates this on execution step 1: the fleet actually carrying #1138 — every member's executor workflow at HEAD triggering on both ready spellings, judged from each repo's own file. Until then a member that has not taken the new stub stops seeing label events the moment the engine writes the canonical ready spelling — latency, not lost work (the hourly scheduler dispatch is the guaranteed delivery), but the plan's ordering exists to avoid even that.
>
> **#1154 is that gate, and it merges this PR itself.** It is a deferred request on the queue: it reads Shepherd's stamp and workflow file, sweeps every member it can enumerate, and merges this only when all of it passes — re-arming daily until then, and parking for a human if it cannot make the reads.

## What flips

- **The constants every writer already uses now hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin. One edit moves every write site: the generator's occurrence wears `task:origin:planned`, a hand-created item `task:origin:ad-hoc`, a marked issue the same, and the stubs' failure issues `task:origin:github` (that one landed in #1138). Their **names** survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it.
- **The dashboard follows** with its own display key for the park column, rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase**: clearing the status *is* the re-ask, so the five messages that said "remove the `needs-human` labels" now say that, from one home.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/queue/       the write constants, the one-label park, origins on
                              every born item, the shared re-queue phrase, and the
                              session/worker briefs that tell an agent what to write
packs/basics/                 the janitor's sweep writes one park label; version bumped
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   the park column gets its own display key; version bumped
packs/claudinite-growth/      writing-tasks states today's vocabulary; version bumped
```

Note on versions: `basics` and `claudinite-dashboard` are bumped **again** here (`.2`). They already moved in #1138, and `pack-version-bumped` compares against `main` — so it could not see that these edits ride a version #1138 has already delivered. Without the second bump they would reach nobody.

## Verification

Re-run after the rebase onto the squashed `main`: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2409 pass, 0 fail; `check_the_work` clean.

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status. Seen to fail with the flip reverted. The 43 test failures the flip caused were all write-assertion churn — updated in place, and the legacy-spelling coverage now lives where it belongs, in the decode tests.

{"number":1157,"title":"Promote portable lessons from Shepherd and TLDR","body":"Refs #99. `canon-curation/growth-promote` run over the local packs of `missingbulb/Shepherd`, `missingbulb/TLDR` and `missingbulb/WIP` (this window's Context — the members whose local packs changed). WIP's local pack is still empty (``), so nothing to read there.

**Six prose additions** (`packs/basics/RULES.md`, `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md`) — all judgment/runtime-behavior items with no reliable static signature a check could carry:

- **Shepherd** → `basics/RULES.md` (Harness-tool contracts) — check first whether an `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided (a loaded rule, a read away, the recommended option being the status quo), and batch every open decision into **one** question.
- **Shepherd** → `basics/RULES.md` (Working discipline) — retiring a system by folding its function into another: verify the *generator* moved, not just its historical output, and check whether the new generator's own inputs retain the same history a carried-over aggregate already holds before dropping it on the assumption "the next run recomputes it."
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — a session scoped to a **single** repo denies a cross-repo call outright, not merely filters; check the session's actual scope, and look for the answer in what you already have (an issue/PR body often already carries it), before spending a call rediscovering the denial. (Sharpens the existing "When access is scoped to an explicit repo list" section with the single-repo case.)
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — `search_code`'s index can lag and silently undercount when enumerating a population across many repos; cross-check against a direct enumeration before trusting it as complete (measured: 3 of 11 affected repos via search alone).
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — after a bulk/fleet-wide sweep, subscribe to **every** PR it leaves open, not a sample — the unsubscribed ones get no activity signal and fall back to real-cost re-polling.
- **Shepherd** → `claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md` — re-run `converge-wiring.mjs --badges` on a pack **rename or removal**, not just on adoption via the `adopt-pack` skill (which already covers the addition case) — otherwise the README's packs badge row goes silently stale and only resurfaces later as a blocking `reference-integrity` finding.

Versions bumped: `basics` 60821.1 → 60821.2, `git-github` 60820.2 → 60821.1, `claudinite-lifecycle` 60821.1 → 60821.2.

**Notable rejections (dedup verified against the current corpus and open PRs, not memory):**

- **TLDR's `comment-class-menu` check** (advisory, catches a `Comment class:` line that declares extra classes via a same-line explanation or a pasted menu) — not promoted. This exact lesson, generalized as `comment-classification-form`, is already proposed in the still-open PR #1021 (from a prior promote run over TLDR). More pointedly: #1114 (2026-08-20, one day before this run) is the owner's own deliberate, measured call to **remove** a check in this same area (`comment-classification.mjs`, 204 blocking firings / 21% of all blocking findings in 31 days) and keep only the prose. Re-adding a check here — even TLDR's narrower, advisory-severity one — reopens a question the owner just settled; it's #1021's (and the owner's) call, not this run's to re-litigate or duplicate.
- **TLDR's `release-root-version-align` check** — TLDR's own local delta over its vendored `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` stub (a repo-root `package.json` alignment step, tied to specific commits/PR numbers). Not portable — stays local.
- **Shepherd's fleet-activity-filtering lesson** (filter the machine's own bookkeeping out of activity rankings, via `isDispatchTitle`) — grounded entirely in Shepherd's own fleet-enforcer role; there is exactly one fleet enforcer, so it isn't reusable by a future project.
- **Shepherd's PR-CI-polling lesson** (poll `get_check_runs`, don't call `enable_pr_auto_merge` before checks start) — already covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "An auto-merge refusal is not a verdict" and "To read a PR's CI result" sections.
- **Shepherd's `search_issues`-by-exact-title lesson** — already covered near-verbatim by `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap and qualify every list/search call" section ("When you already know the exact title, don't search at all — list and match it yourself").

Verified: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2406/2406 green (unshallowed the checkout first; one pre-existing failure from the shallow default clone cleared before any of this PR's changes were applied). `check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 68 advisory, none touching the files this PR changes.

[{"sha":"6a7ba12ed0c89f84e2008e9ccc4e2a80d64fffcd","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/6a7ba12ed0c89f84e2008e9ccc4e2a80d64fffcd","message":"Vendor export-build-vars.mjs with the rest of the static-site set

The standing static-site-vendoring record materializes the read-site-config
action and its read-config.mjs but not the exporter beside them, so a repo that
declares build_vars never self-heals onto a copy that honours it — the very
case sw/release-workflows reports as blocking, with no route to green but a
hand copy.

Refs #1150","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T09:28:33Z"}},{"sha":"ed7248e242d4300b85725a29e4b1780bcae19035","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/ed7248e242d4300b85725a29e4b1780bcae19035","message":"The version bump belongs to the change, not to the release flow

Both release standards wrote the version themselves — the extension's daily run
patch-bumped and pushed to main before packaging, the site's publish reusable
computed the date-anchored version and pushed it before tagging. So the version
a reviewer saw on a PR was never the version that shipped, and the one push a
pipeline made to main unattended was the one that could fail non-fast-forward
and strand a release. Claudinite holds the opposite line on itself, in
pack-version-bumped and engine-release-record; these two packs now hold it too.

A work-scope check per pack, gated on the repo shipping the pipeline and scoped
by the repo's OWN declaration of what ships:

  cer/version-bumped  a change touching ship_paths raises the manifest version
  sw/version-bumped   a change touching the publish set raises version_files

Each is silent on a change that ships nothing, and defers to the neighbouring
check (cer/version-sync, sw/version-scheme) on an off-scheme version rather
than reporting it twice.

The pipelines stop writing versions. Both now ask the release list whether the
version on main has been released yet, instead of diffing files against a tag:
idempotent by construction, so a failed run retries with nothing to undo, and a
push carrying an already-released version is a clean no-op. The extension's
create-package already worked this way; the daily run just loses its bump job.

What is left over is the bump that belongs to no single change, so each
orchestrator gains a dispatch for it — mode: bump with part: minor|major for the
extension, bump: major for the site (the date-anchored scheme has no minor). Each
calls a new vendored reusable that raises the version, pushes, and lets the
ordinary release path ship it.

Supporting moves: the two bump scripts gain the parts they now have to write and
a --print reader (so nothing else has to know where a version lives), the
extension's read-release-config exports a pure parse for the check to share, and
the chrome bump action keeps its bump-extension-patch path — vendored into every
extension repo, a rename would strand the old copy with nothing able to remove it.

Refs #1150","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T09:28:48Z"}},{"sha":"e52fc018bcca79381daf3202d9ed4c55e9c4a3b8","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/e52fc018bcca79381daf3202d9ed4c55e9c4a3b8","message":"Retire basics' bump-version skill; the phrase goes to the packs that answer it

The skill had become a two-entry routing table: after the bump moved into the
change, its whole body was "for an extension repo see chrome-store-releases,
for a site repo see static-site-releases". Three things wrong with that.

The links dangle for most members. computeVendorSet builds the vendor set from
the DECLARED entries, so a repo declaring basics without static-website never
receives packs/static-website/ — and basics is declared everywhere while those
two are declared by a handful. Nothing catches it: pack-independence bars
cross-pack imports, not doc links.

It goes stale on another pack's schedule — this file was rewritten one commit
ago for no reason but that those two packs changed.

And it was never the general answer anyway: app-store-release and
play-store-release carry no versioning content at all, so the router covered
exactly the two packs that already owned their bump story end to end.

What it genuinely bought was the trigger phrase — "bump version" appeared
verbatim in the skill index only here. That moves into the description of each
skill that owns an answer, where it routes to the pack that has one and only in
a repo that declares it. A repo declaring neither has no version scheme, and
"which files carry the version?" is the right answer there, not a stub.

Refs #1150","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T11:10:12Z"}},{"sha":"6d7a36a50f330543cab081948584ba7d437a7795","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/6d7a36a50f330543cab081948584ba7d437a7795","message":"Keep the version line to the version, not a changelog beside it

The three pack manifests this change touched carried a running list of what
each past version delivered. That history is the git log's, not a comment's.
basics' first entry stated a real invariant — a migration record's declared
version against this one — so that survives as what it is, a contract on the
field, with the changelog framing dropped.

[{"sha":"eef03a4c7cd0cd16b2a3347610fdf7643e6c5528","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/eef03a4c7cd0cd16b2a3347610fdf7643e6c5528","message":"Decode every label spelling, and trigger the executor on both

The read half of the unified `task:status:`/`task:origin:` vocabulary. Labels
are stored data — an open item wears whatever the engine that filed it wrote,
and members converge on their own schedules — so every reader now goes through
one decode pass (`statusOf`) that maps every spelling ever written straight to
today's, and nothing compares a label literally any more.

Nothing writes a canonical status yet. The ensure-list carries them regardless,
because a label that does not exist 422s the write that would apply it and the
ensure pass reaches a member a converge before the flip does. Transitions leave
a status through `apply-status`, which clears every spelling of it rather than
the one this engine happens to write — the flip is then six constants changing.

The executor workflow's event trigger is the one surface where both vocabularies
must appear at once (a trigger names label strings literally, nothing decodes
there), so it accepts both ready spellings, in the stub and in the canon's own
copy; both workflows now file their failure issues with an origin and a park.

Refs #1119","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T00:44:24Z"}},{"sha":"e2b554163485346a4834b4c73388f7088c692e09","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/e2b554163485346a4834b4c73388f7088c692e09","message":"The marked issue IS the item — one-issue requests

The request mode's shadow work item is gone. A person marks an ordinary issue
`task:origin:ad-hoc`; adoption appends the machine block to that issue's own body
and applies the first status; the whole lifecycle then plays out where the person
is already looking. Any status — live, parked or terminal — holds the mark until
somebody clears it, which collapses the old model's two retry levers into one and
makes an impatient re-ask mid-run structurally nothing: there is no second object
to supersede, and no prior item to wait on.

The parameters move with it. They rode write-gated labels; they ride the person's
own text now (`Task:`, `Model:`, `Automerge:`, beside `Blocked-by:` and
`Not-before:`), re-read at every adoption and honoured only for an author with
push access — read from the collaborators-permission API, never the payload's
association. An ungated ask still runs, at the defaults, and is told so.

`Task: /` is new: which task a mark asks for, defaulting to the
built-in implementer. An id this repo does not carry is not adopted at all — the
mark waits, as it waits on an engine too old to carry the mode.

Nothing closes somebody's issue any more: a refusal's terminal status stands on
the open issue, because the run's verdict is not the issue's validity. The
`claude-*` vocabulary is read forever — `claude-task` still marks, a draining
shadow item still writes back to the issue it names — and written never.

Refs #1119","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T01:03:10Z"}},{"sha":"6e6529bb894554712606ce5cac41f9f65b64e3b1","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/6e6529bb894554712606ce5cac41f9f65b64e3b1","message":"Read a marked issue's task off the path its block names

A marked issue's title is the person's own, so every reader that took the task
from the title had a hole in it: the janitor's stale-ready rule skipped every
request run (one nobody picked up would have sat ready forever), and the
dashboard rendered them as items belonging to no task.

`taskIdFromPath` is the parse both now use — a worker path in either home, under
either root. Anything that must know the task exists at HEAD still resolves the
path against the discovered set instead.

Refs #1119","author":{"name":"Claude","email":"noreply@anthropic.com","date":"2026-08-21T01:05:49Z"}},{"sha":"53a20383d12d7c16d6d8211d988cbde3f3d06d7f","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/53a20383d12d7c16d6d8211d988cbde3f3d06d7f","message":"Fold add-packs onto the marked issue

A member's add-packs work list was a labelled issue plus a `wake:` dispatch that
told the member's scheduler to run a task which then went looking for that issue.
The work list is a marked issue now: the enforcer applies `task:origin:ad-hoc`
and names the member task in the body's `Task:` field, so the member's own
scheduler run adopts it and the issue becomes the item the agent runs on.

What goes with the dispatch: the member task's code-work gate and its worker,
which existed only because a woken standing item had no idea why it was awake.
What stays: the label, the two converged titles, and the JSON block — the
protocol both sides still read.

Three things the fold has to get right, and does. The mark is created in the
member before it is applied, since a refused label is a work list nobody runs. A
re-forced ask keeps the machine block the member wrote and clears the status,
which is the sanctioned re-ask. And a second work list in a member names the
first in `Blocked-by:` — two lists are two items of one task, which nothing else
serializes, and two sessions on one declaration is two conflicting PRs.

The dispatch that remains is latency, not delivery: an ordinary scheduler run so
the mark is adopted in a minute rather than at the next hour, and a member that
refuses it is reported rather than failing the sweep.

{"number":1158,"title":"claudinite-dashboard: usage-backed data plane, per-repo redesign, repo/fleet modes — and retire fleet-usage","body":"Tracking issue for the dashboard redesign. The plan below is ordered by what blocks (out-of-band setup → one review pass over a PR stack → unattended execution → destructive tail), not by subject. Once agreed, this body is append-only.

## First, the question asked: is `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` redundant?

**Yes — with one catch that sequences the removal.**

- The sweep is a **stateless full recompute, a pure function of the members' current files** (its own README says so). It holds **no longer history** than the members: each member's week rows are append-once and never pruned, so the member files are the complete record and the fleet file adds no depth.
- **Nothing in the canon reads it.** Grep finds only the task's own files, its tests, docs and the `.gitattributes` entry. It was built for fleet-wide analysis by a human/agent reading one file — the fleet dashboard is now that reader, better.
- The **access argument is real and favors dropping**: the aggregate in Shepherd shows anyone with Shepherd read the whole fleet's numbers, while the dashboard reads each member's file *as the viewer* — a repo you can't read renders "not visible to you". Per-repo files are the permission-correct source.
- **Catch 1 — it is currently the fleet dashboard's roster.** Shepherd's declaration reads `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"`. The member list is the one thing genuinely fleet-shaped in it, so the fleet page needs a replacement roster source *before* the file goes (PR 3 below).
- Catch 2 — the `coverage` census (absent / dormant / out-of-scope, with reasons) is the only other content member files can't hold. The fleet page derives it live: a rostered repo with no readable usage file **is** the absent row, and `dormant` is read off the member's own declaration.

So: drop the task and the file — sequenced after the fleet page stops reading it (the tail, below).

## Design decisions

1. **Fresh vs past split.** *Fresh* per page load: repo metadata, head sha, the open-issue page, the runs list — all ETag-revalidated (a 304 is free), target **~5 requests warm, all 304s** on the per-repo page. *Past*: one blob read of `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`, cached by head sha — **zero requests while `main` is unmoved**. Nothing else reaches back in time over the API.
2. **usage.GENERATED.json v3 stays raw data**, not UI-shaped: per-hour and per-day series with per-item detail preserved, so future UI changes re-render without re-folding. Readers accept v2 (legacy at the door): an absent series renders as a stated gap, never a guessed zero — the #1001 rule.
3. **Freshness provenance**: a `generated` stamp in the file, excluded from the worker's unchanged-compare exactly as the fleet file's `generatedAt` already is — so it reads "when the data last moved" and a quiet repo still opens no PR. The head-commit date the page already holds is the upper bound beside it.
4. **usage-fold goes hourly, gated on movement** — signals `commits` + `conversationLogs` + runs movement; a quiet hour declines. The REST-read families stay incremental past their watermarks; day recomputes stay local-git and free.
5. **Mode is structural, no new config key**: a declaration with a roster source (`owner` or legacy `rosterFile`) is a **fleet-dashboard** deployment, anything else is a **repo-dashboard** one; `build-site.mjs` mounts that landing. Nothing to ask at adoption, nothing to misconfigure.
6. **Fleet roster = live enumeration as the viewer**: config `owner` (+ existing `exclude`), membership = a readable `.claudinite-checks.json` at head (sha-cached, so the probe is amortized). This also honors the standing "no repo list exists anywhere in canon code" decision. Fallback if enumeration proves too costly at fleet size: a slim `roster.GENERATED.json` from a Shepherd fleet task (the sanctioned daily auto-merged GENERATED-file shape) — not built unless measurement says so.

{"number":1188,"title":"Nothing prunes an absorbed pack's leftover directory from a member's mount","body":"Blocked-by: #1187

Model: opus

When a pack is **absorbed** into another (`chrome-extension-release` → `chrome-extension`, `github-actions` → `git-github`, `firebase-release` → `firebase` — #1057, #1079), its directory stays in every member's mount forever. The pack flow "replaces a declared pack's tree wholesale but never removes a tree that has stopped being declared" (`engine/migrations/2026-08-19-pack-renames/migration.mjs`), and no migration record covers the absorptions — grep finds none.

After #1187 those leftovers are inert rather than fatal, so this is dead weight, not breakage: a complete, loadable copy of a retired pack sitting beside its survivor in seven members' trees.

**Why a rename record doesn't fit.** The rename records work by `aliases`, which *move* the legacy directory onto the canonical path, and depend on "the canonical side does not exist yet" — for an absorption the survivor's directory is already there, so the move cannot apply. The action here is a **delete**, which the record vocabulary has no shape for today.

**Done looks like**: a member's converge removes `.claudinite/shared/packs//` for each absorbed pack, and a member that already converged past the record still gets there. Confirm against a real member tree, not only a fixture — the same way #1186 was confirmed.

**Ruled out**: doing it inside #1187. That change unfreezes the fleet and stays scoped to the loader; a destructive sweep over members' trees is a separate concern with its own risk.

Worth checking while here whether the absorbed ids can start coming out of `RENAMED_PACKS` — its own retirement rule is "no member's declaration and no member's stamped `packVersions` still carries that spelling", which several members still do.

{"number":1174,"title":"fleet-baseline can only force `update` — there is no lever for any other task fleet-wide","body":"`fleet-baseline` is the fleet's only forcing lever, and it hard-codes what it forces:

```js
// packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs
export const FORCED_TASK = 'update';
```

Everything underneath it is already generic — `fireScheduler(gh, fullName, ref, taskId)` takes the id as an argument, and the member-side `planWake` accepts a whitespace/comma-separated list of `task` or `pack/task` ids and *creates* the standing item when one is missing. Only the constant is fixed.

So "force task X across the fleet" has exactly one route today: dispatch each member's `claudinite-scheduler.yml` yourself with `wake: X`. That needs Actions-write on every member, which is the credential `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` exists to hold and which an interactive session scoped to a handful of repos does not have. The alternative — attaching every member to the session — is per-repo manual work, which reliably does not happen.

Surfaced doing #1158's "force `usage-fold` fleet-wide" step. It cost nothing there: the converge `fleet-baseline` forces lands a commit on each member's default branch, and that commit is exactly what `usage-fold`'s movement precondition gates on, so forcing `update` forced the fold one hop later by accident. The next task that wants a fleet-wide force will not be so lucky.

**Shape of the fix** (the lever's `README` already documents the parameter-bag pattern this would join): a `WAKE` context parameter beside the existing `REPOS` / `DRY_RUN` / `INCLUDE_DORMANT`, defaulting to `update` so every existing item keeps its meaning, passed through to `fireScheduler` and named in the run summary. The summary line already reads *"Asked each covered member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` to wake its `update` item"* — it would just stop being a constant.

Two things to get right, both learned the hard way in this repo:

- **The protocol spans repos.** The dispatch input is read by each member's own vendored scheduler stub, so a new spelling has to be one every fielded stub already understands. `wake` itself is unchanged here — only which id travels in it — so this should be safe, but it is the class of change that broke Shepherd's only caller in #929.
- **A parameter that stops being read must fail loudly** (#974). If `WAKE` is added, an item naming a task no declared pack owns must land in the summary's `failed` list, not dispatch `update` silently because the name did not resolve.

Not urgent — nothing is blocked on it — but it is a hole in the fleet's control surface that is invisible until someone needs it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1174","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-21T15:19:37Z","updated_at":"2026-08-21T15:19:37Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1169,"title":"Dissolve docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md into the packs that own its subjects","body":"The owner's read, and it holds up against the tree: this design doc collapses into the pack that collects the signals and into the dashboard. It is 769 lines describing a pipeline that is now built, and the canon's own rule for that is already written — *behaviour belongs in the module header and the pack README*, not in a doc that has to be kept in step with both.

The evidence, section by section (line counts from `2026-08-21`):

| § | Lines | Where it already lives, or should |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Where knowledge lives | 16 | A standing architectural rule ("the canon knows mechanisms, never repos") — belongs with the local pack's standing decisions, not in one initiative's doc |
| 2 Sources of truth | 18 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` |
| 3 Capture (3.1–3.5) | ~100 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` already carries the capture lifecycle and retention almost verbatim; `capture-log.mjs`'s header carries the rest. **§3.4 (capturing an unattended session, where no SessionEnd hook fires) and §3.5 (the ordering constraint) are the one part with no other home** — they go into the pack README beside the lifecycle they belong to |
| 4.1 Check activations | 101 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "The check failures are the win" and `fold-usage.mjs`'s header both carry the three marks, the CI-in-the-loop rule and the floor property |
| 4.2 Task invocations | 69 | Describes the retired slot-scheduler census. Keep two sentences of it as history in `usage-fold/README.md` (which already has them) and drop the rest |
| 4.3 Exec statuses | 16 | `usage-fold/README.md` |
| 5 The per-repo aggregate + shape | 146 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md` and `usage-format.mjs`'s header |
| 6 The fleet aggregate | 63 | Superseded; **deleted outright** — the task it describes goes in #1166 |
| 7 Consumers | 40 | Split: the promotion-ladder half to `claudinite-growth/README.md`, the reader half to `claudinite-dashboard/README.md` |
| 8 TTLs | 12 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` (it already states retention) |
| 9 Failure modes | 45 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "Failure is visible, never silent" |
| 10 + the two later rounds | 57 | Owner decisions with their rationale. These are the doc's only irreplaceable content — move them to the local pack's standing decisions, where a session actually reads them |

So the shape of the change: **almost nothing is written fresh.** Two sections move (§3.4/§3.5, and the decision record), one is deleted, and the rest is verified as already-covered and then dropped. If a section turns out *not* to be covered where this table claims, write it into the pack — do not keep the doc alive for it.

## The references are the real work

Eight files point into this doc by section number, and a dangling `§` pointer is worse than no pointer:

```
engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs          §3.3
engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs               §4.2
packs/claudinite-growth/session-end.mjs       (unnumbered)
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/task.mjs        §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/worker.mjs      §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/fold-usage.mjs  §4, §5
docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md         §4.2 and one unnumbered
```

Each becomes either a pointer to the pack README section that absorbed it, or — better where the sentence was only citing itself — nothing at all. Use the `repo-text-sweeps` skill; grep for `skill-usage-metrics` afterwards and confirm zero hits outside history.

## Done looks like

`docs/skill-usage-metrics/` is gone; no file in the tree references it; the owner decision record is in the local pack's standing decisions; §3.4 and §3.5's content is in `claudinite-growth/README.md`; the full suite and `check_the_world` are green.

## Worth deciding while doing it

The same argument applies to the other five `docs/*/DESIGN.md` — `tasks-dispatch` alone is 1,958 lines and is cited from dozens of module headers. **Do not sweep them in this change.** If the pattern holds, say so in a comment here and let the owner decide separately; a 4,300-line doc migration is not something to discover mid-run.

{"number":1166,"title":"Retire the fleet-usage task and usage-fleet.GENERATED.json","body":"The destructive tail of #1158. The fleet-wide usage aggregate has no reader left: it was a stateless recompute over the members' own files, it held no longer history than they do (their week rows are append-once and never pruned), and the fleet dashboard now reads each member's file directly — as the viewer, which is also the permission-correct source. Its `coverage` census is derived live: a rostered member with no usage file *is* the absent row.

The last thing it was needed for was being the fleet page's **roster**, which #1165 replaces with live enumeration of a configured `owner`.

## The change

In this repo (the canon):

- delete `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/` — the task, `worker.mjs`, `aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs`, their tests and the task README;
- remove its row from the `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` pack README's task catalog;
- bump the sheepdog pack's version, with the reason in the version comment;
- check `.gitattributes` for a `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json merge=ours` entry and drop it if this repo carries one;
- grep the corpus for `usage-fleet` and `fleet-usage` and clean up what is left — `docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md` §6 already carries a superseded note, so update it to past tense rather than adding a second one.

In Shepherd (a separate change, by whoever holds that repo): delete `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` and its `.gitattributes` entry. The file is harmless while it sits there, so this is tidiness rather than a blocker.

## Done looks like

The canon carries no `fleet-usage` task and no code that reads or writes a fleet-wide usage aggregate; the sheepdog pack's README and version reflect that; the full suite and `check_the_world` are green; and Shepherd's fleet dashboard still renders (it reads members' files, not this one).

## Do not start before

Both preconditions below are real, not formalities. The task must not be deleted while anything still reads its output.

1. **#1165 is merged** — that is what stops the fleet page reading `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` as its roster.
2. **Shepherd's `claudinite-dashboard` declaration has been flipped** from `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"` to `"owner": "missingbulb"`. Until that lands, Shepherd's deployed page is still resolving its member list from this file, and deleting the task would freeze that list at whatever it last held. Verify it at Shepherd's HEAD before touching anything here.

If the second is not true yet, close nothing and change nothing: comment saying which precondition is outstanding and leave this issue for the next pick.

{"number":1161,"title":"Verify in production: a static site still redeploys now the pipeline never bumps","body":"#1151 took the version write out of the `static-website` release pipeline. The publish reusable
used to compute `..` and push it to `main` before tagging; it now writes nothing
and instead asks whether the version already on `main` has a release yet. The bump moved into the
change that touches the publish set (`sw/version-bumped`), and the deliberate major is a
`bump: major` dispatch calling a new vendored reusable (`static-site-bump-version.yml`).

**Why this could not be watched at merge time.** The checks are unit-tested and the vendoring
round-trip is covered, but nothing in this repo executes a GitHub Actions workflow. The release
trigger changed from a publish-set file diff to a version-versus-release-list test, and that only
runs in a site repo after the nightly converge materialises the new stubs. Its failure mode is
silent in the direction that matters: a wrong condition means the site quietly stops

{"number":1153,"title":"Adoption leaves the queue's agent hop unwired — no routine, no taskScheduler.endpoints, and no handover","body":"Adopting Claudinite on a fresh member lands the scheduler and executor workflows, the task declarations and the queue, but nothing in the adoption flow creates the member's invocation routine or declares `taskScheduler.endpoints`. The result is a member that looks fully adopted and drains only its code-work tasks — every task with an agentic phase fails at the hand-off:

> Could not start an agent session: this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "default" (taskScheduler.endpoints)

Seen on `missingbulb/WIP`, adopted 2026-08-20: four work items (missingbulb/WIP#12, missingbulb/WIP#20, missingbulb/WIP#24, missingbulb/WIP#27) were claimed, handed off, refused, and labelled `needs-human` before anyone looked. The code-work-only tasks completed normally, so the queue's own signals all read healthy.

Two distinct gaps, and the second is the one that let it sit unnoticed for a day:

1. **`adopt-claudinite` never wires the endpoint.** It asks no adoption question about invocation, writes no `taskScheduler.endpoints` entry, and names no secret — so `resolveEndpoint` fails on the very first agentic item of a new member's life. Either the skill should walk the operator through creating the routine and declaring the endpoint, or a member with no endpoint should fail loudly at adoption time rather than at the first hand-off.
2. **No handover issue is filed for the part a human must do.** The routine's API token and the repo Actions secret are human-only steps, and the canon's own rule is that such a step gets its own issue with a checkbox per step and what breaks while each is off. Adoption files nothing — the gap exists only as three bot comments on a dead work item, which is exactly where nobody reads it.

Worth deciding alongside this: whether a per-member routine is the intended shape at all, or whether adoption should point new members at the fleet routine by default and let a member opt into its own.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1153","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-21T09:47:05Z","updated_at":"2026-08-21T09:47:05Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1149,"title":"converge-item.mjs cannot run from an MCP-only agent session","body":"`engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` step 6 tells the session executing a work item to run:

```
node /scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome ... --summary ...
```

directly as a subprocess. That script (via `engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`'s `makeGh`) talks to `api.github.com` straight over `fetch`, authorized with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN` — the Action-side credential, per the DESIGN comment atop `gh.mjs`: "engine/scheduler/ is the one place that legitimately uses the Action's GITHUB_TOKEN — everything session-side stays MCP-only."

But `queue/instructions.md` step 6 *is* session-side — it is the procedure every agent session follows to converge the one work item it was fired for (a Claude Code session, not an Actions job). This session's own system prompt states plainly it has no `gh` CLI and no direct GitHub API access, and must use the GitHub MCP server tools for all GitHub interactions. Confirmed live on this run (#1097):

- `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is unset by default in this session (`converge-item: GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`).
- Setting it and calling the script directly returns a 403 straight from the GitHub REST API: `{"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization."}` — a policy boundary, not a fixable env-var wrinkle.

This is the same class of break as #1133: a script written for the Actions-job execution context (`gh.mjs`'s `makeGh`) silently fails once the same work runs inside an MCP-only agent session — except here the break isn't silent, it's a hard stop on the one step every work item's session-side execution must perform: convergence. As written, no work item picked up by an agent session (`queue/instructions.md`'s normal path) can converge in code — it either gets hand-converged (which `instructions.md` explicitly says not to do) or sits stuck wearing `task:agent` until the janitor's 3h agent-leash reclaims it as dead.

The repo already has the right shape for this split: `deliver-pr.md` (AGENT lane, MCP-backed) beside `land-pr.mjs` (CODE lane, Action-side `gh.mjs`) for PR delivery. `converge-item.mjs` needs the same — an MCP-backed convergence path `queue/instructions.md` can actually invoke from a session, mirroring what `convergeItem()` already does (comment, swap labels, close/park, release dependents, request write-back) but over `mcp__github__*` tools instead of `gh.mjs`.

Observed on #1097 (`Request: #1095`): the actual requested work completed and was verified successfully — #1095 was checked and closed with the evidence. Only this item's own code-side convergence failed, for the reason above. {"number":1133,"title":"converge-item.mjs needs a real GITHUB_TOKEN the queue's own sessions don't have","body":"`engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` step 6 tells every work-item session to converge by running:

```bash
node /scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome ... --summary '...'
```

`converge-item.mjs` reads and writes the issue over a direct `api.github.com` fetch, authenticated with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN` (`engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`). That's fine for the retired executor mechanism, which ran as the Action's own job step with `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` set in its shell (`.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`). But the sessions the *current* queue dispatches to are Claude Code cloud/web sessions (`claude.ai/code/session_...`, per the hand-off comment on each work item) — and that session type's platform policy is MCP-only GitHub access: no `gh` CLI, no direct API calls. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` such a session does see in its shell env is not a GitHub credential at all (14 chars, `prox...` prefix — a proxy artifact), so the script's very first call (`readIssue`) fails with a 401 before it ever reaches its own judgment logic.

Hit this converging #1129 (implementing #1124): `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=missingbulb/Claudinite node engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue 1129 --outcome done --summary '...'` exited 1 with `converge-item: #1129 could not be read`. Worked around it by replicating the script's side effects (comment with the same `claudinite-task-exec` record line, `task:agent`→`task:done` swap, close as completed) directly over the `mcp__github__*` tools instead — same end state, just not "in code" as instructed. Skipped only the `readyDependents` release, which `readiness.mjs` itself documents as safe to skip for a close performed outside the script (the hourly scheduler run is the backstop).

The retired `executor.md` already solved the same problem for a different script shape: its `needs-issue` verdict has the session fetch the one issue it needs over MCP, save the raw JSON, and hand it to the shell via `--issue-json ` rather than have the shell fetch it itself. `converge-item.mjs` has no such path — it only ever fetches and writes live. Given it writes too (comment, label, close), an `--issue-json` equivalent alone wouldn't fully solve it; it'd need either a write-side MCP shim as well, or a documented "no working token → do these exact steps over your GitHub tools instead" fallback in `instructions.md` step 6, mirroring what every session hitting this will otherwise rediscover from scratch.

Every future `implement-request` (and any other queue task converging through this same step 6) will hit this identically in this session type — this isn't specific to #1124/#1129.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1133","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-20T22:03:49Z","updated_at":"2026-08-21T04:33:47Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1050,"title":"Collapse the `needs-human` pair into one label — by 2026-08-26","body":"#1049 landed the triage split **additively**: every park wears `needs-human` *and* one of `task:needs-human-{action,decision,approval,failure}`. {"number":1096,"title":"Every executor run logs `could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404`","body":"Every executor run on canon prints this before doing anything:

```
! could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404
```

Seen on `main`'s run [32368276774](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32368276774/job/96422660810) and on a branch run of #1089 at the same minute, so it is **not** from that PR — it is standing behavior on every run, and has been long enough that nobody reads the line any more.

`ensureLabels(gh, repo, [...QUEUE_LABELS, ...REQUEST_LABELS])` is the caller; `AUTOMERGE_LABEL` (`claude-automerge`) is in `REQUEST_LABELS`. The reconcile is fail-soft, which is why the run stays green — but the label is the asker's merge authorization (`MERGE_IF_NARROW`), read from a write-gated label at adoption. A label that cannot be reconciled is one that may not exist in the picker for a person to apply, which would make that authorization unreachable rather than merely unstamped.

Worth establishing before deciding the fix:

- whether the label exists on the repo at all, or the 404 is the *update* path failing on a label that does exist,
- whether the same line appears on members (it would be the same code, so probably),
- whether anything has ever successfully read `claude-automerge` off an issue here.

> **Mode is structural, no new config key**: a declaration with a roster source (`owner` or legacy `rosterFile`) is a **fleet-dashboard** deployment, anything else is a **repo-dashboard** one … Nothing to ask at adoption, nothing to misconfigure.

"Anything else" is a default, not a structural derivation — and it collides with the standing decision to *avoid a default; require the value explicitly*. The owner caught it on Canary's declaration, which was a bare `"claudinite-dashboard"`: repo mode was what saying nothing produced.

The failure it allows is specific. The inference cannot tell **"this repo only"** from **"the fleet, whose roster source went missing"** — a dropped key, a renamed artifact, an enumeration never configured. Both present as "no roster", and the second publishes a one-repo dashboard that looks intentional. `build-site.mjs` already warned about exactly this shape without being able to stop it.

Amended to: **a deployment states its mode.** `mode` is `"repo"` or `"fleet"`, required, no default; the build refuses an absent mode and a mode that contradicts the config in either direction. It costs the one adoption question decision 5 was avoiding, which is the right price — both answers are ordinary, neither is rarer, and there is no value here that is right for nearly every project.

Tracked in #1179, pack change in #1182, and the two live deployments state their mode in Shepherd#142 (`fleet`) and ClaudiniteCanary#160 (`repo`).

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](../packs/) and [skills/](../skills/) corpus); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([../skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md](../skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](../packs/) and [skills/](../skills/) corpus); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. ## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. - **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.

- 2026-08-21T0958Z--issue-1119--f1177d57-856d-5be7-9dab-d754fa2645f8.jsonl

Report per file: a one-line summary of what the session did, and EITHER "nothing extractable" OR a candidate lesson stated as one distilled imperative rule in this repo's terse voice, with the concrete evidence (quote a short phrase, cite real timestamps for any wall-time claim), and your judgment on whether it's already covered in RULES.md (quote the closest existing bullet if so). Be honest that most sessions will likely yield nothing — that's the expected, common outcome; don't manufacture lessons. Keep your final report tight. Do not edit any files or post anything to GitHub — this is read-only research, I will decide what (if anything) to land.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name.
