A pass is all three, read from the repos' own files and issues — never from a run conclusion. Then, and only then, merge #1152.
Not-before: 2026-08-22T10:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

## The playbook — the run decides nothing beyond what is written here

1. **Read `In-production-when:`** against Shepherd's real files. A merge is not the condition and neither is elapsed time.
2. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.
3. **Live** → run `Verify:`.
   - **Cannot enumerate members** (no fleet token, the search refuses, the repo scope does not reach them): park this item `task:status:needs-human-action` saying exactly which read you could not make. Never treat an empty or partial sweep as a pass — a uniform clean answer from a rate-limited or scope-blocked probe looks exactly like a healthy fleet.
   - **A member is behind, or an item looks stuck** → comment here with the repo, the file you read and what it said; comment the same on #1119; leave this issue open and push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`. Do not merge.
   - **All three pass** → go to 4.
4. **Merge #1152.** Confirm first that it is open, its base is `main`, its head's checks are green and GitHub reports it mergeable; if any of those is false, park `task:status:needs-human-decision` saying which. Otherwise squash-merge it with the title `Write the canonical spellings (#1152)`.
5. **Report and hand back.** Comment on #1119: what you read, per member; that #1152 merged; and that execution step 2 remains — force `fleet-baseline` with `follow` and watch a member's fresh scheduler cycle file items wearing only the new spellings. Then close this issue as completed.

If the verification finds the fault instead — a member the decode broke — reopen #1119 with what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it, comment here linking that, and close this issue as completed. Finding the fault is this run doing its job.

{"name":"mcp__github__issue_write","input":{"method":"create","owner":"missingbulb","repo":"Claudinite","title":"Migration plans: write everything up front, then chain the execution steps","body":"Owner, 2026-08-21: the migration-planning flow should be built around continuation tasks — write all the code early including the cleanup, take approval for all of it at once, and wire each step automatically onto the tail of the previous step's validation rather than onto anyone's memory.

Today `writing-migration-plans` gets two thirds of the way there: it front-loads the out-of-band setup and collapses the review gates into one stacked-PR pass. Two gaps remain, and this session hit both while running #1119:

- **The stack stops at the first gate.** The cleanup and the destructive tail are filed as *work to write later*, so the code that retires a shim is written by whoever remembers, months on, with a fresh approval to pay for.
- **Execution steps are a checklist.** The skill says they "can be run at will, in one sitting" — true only when nothing has to become observable in between, which is almost never in a fleet migration. In practice each one waits, and a wait written as a plan bullet is a wait that depends on a person coming back.

The fix is the ordering, not new machinery: everything is written and approved in one pass, and every step after that approval is a queued continuation on the ad-hoc lane, armed on the previous step's **verification** and closing only when its own check passed.
"}}

1	# Claudinite — the canon's own non-portable working rules
2	
3	Lessons specific to working on the canon itself. Anything true for repos beyond this one belongs in
4	the shared canon under `packs/`/`skills/` instead. The `growth-extract` task appends here, each
5	lesson at the strongest mechanism available — a check where the rule is deterministic, else prose.
6	
7	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
8	
9	- **Wanting a rule about what the `packs/` tree may reference** — declare and configure the
10	  `barriers` pack, extending it generically if a capability is missing. Never write standalone
11	  code that checks packs-tree segregation.
12	
13	- **Writing a `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md`** — the end state and its rationale only, with
14	  alternatives and their drawbacks; never requests, prior-state narrative, or owner opinions.
15	  The migration is work, not a document: its phased plan, status and remaining work live in the
16	  tracking issue (`writing-migration-plans`), never in a sibling `MIGRATION.md`.
17	
18	- **Ending a session on unfinished work** — write the state into the tracking issue. The
19	  owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so anything else is lost; never compose a hand-off
20	  prompt.
21	
22	- **Designing anything that spans repos** — split it: a self-contained per-repo half in the
23	  canon, the aggregation half as a Shepherd fleet task. No repo list exists anywhere in canon
24	  code; Shepherd enumerates members at runtime. A derived fleet artifact lands there as a daily
25	  auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file, never a commit to its `main`.
26	
27	- **Choosing a value right for nearly every project** — keep it in the pack's own code: ask
28	  nothing at adoption, write nothing into the member's config. Read config as optional — an
29	  unset key means the default, never "misconfigured".
30	
31	- **Needing a member to flip a platform setting or hold a wider credential** — last resort:
32	  per-repo manual work reliably does not happen, and the capability then dies silently in every
33	  repo nobody configured. Prefer the route that works with the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and
34	  neutralise a blocking platform behaviour's *effect* rather than asking for the platform to be
35	  reconfigured. Where nothing weaker can work (`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`), name the exact scope and
36	  have the automation report when it is missing rather than degrade silently.
37	
38	- **Landing a change to what members receive** — force delivery in the same session only when
39	  *"will it work on every repo?"* is a live question: the answer turns on how members differ —
40	  engine flow, a contract their own files must satisfy, a stub or workflow, a migration record, a
41	  new config key. Then drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, report per member unasked,
42	  and attach the repos that verification needs rather than offering to; a dispatch is not a result,
43	  and 204 means queued. Where the change is uniform by construction — prose, a doc, a move of
44	  something nothing executes from the mount — the nightly converge *is* the delivery, and forcing
45	  buys noise rather than assurance.
46	
47	- **Retiring a field, option or module** — `@deprecated` on its definition, plus a comment at
48	  each sanctioned holdout's declaration site saying why it still carries the field. Never a
49	  bespoke conformance check for a deprecation. Keep the contract validating the lingering field.
50	
51	- **Wanting a `.claudinite-checks.json` entry's config validated** — that is a real JSON Schema
52	  the file points at with `$schema`, checked by ordinary tooling. Never a coded per-pack
53	  validation vocabulary or a bespoke `configSchema` type system on the manifest — built and
54	  reverted in #919 ("That's why we have schemas").
55	
56	- **Wanting to share logic between two sibling packs** — never put it in `engine/`, which breaks
57	  the package-manager model, and never make one pack depend on the other, which is what breaks
58	  pack independence. First check whether the sharing is even necessary — self-describing data
59	  (each side states its own field vocabulary) can remove the need to interpret another pack's
60	  format at all. Where identical code is still needed, consider duplicating it, possibly with a
61	  drift guard; sometimes duplication between packs is fine (#959: "why do you even need a drift
62	  guard? Just write the json. Don't overkill.").
63	
64	- **Surfacing a number a human reads as a report card** (a dashboard tile, a digest, a fleet
65	  rollup) — never a monotonic cumulative total, which says nothing about today, and never a figure
66	  nothing measures (no estimated hours saved, no score). Report a **window against the previous
67	  window**. Where a field can't be had from the reads already being made, name it as absent in the
68	  surface's own note rather than approximating it: a stated gap is information, a guess is not
69	  (owner, #1001). Before windowing a count, check whether it is built from an event log or from a
70	  point-in-time **stamp**: windowing a stamp-derived figure (e.g. "members that converged last
71	  week", counted from each member's single last-converge date) can read a steady, healthy
72	  population as declining purely from where stamps land relative to the window boundary — reserve
73	  the window-over-window shape for counts genuinely built from things that happened inside the
74	  window (#1008).
75	
76	- **Classifying an issue or work item by deriving it structurally from other live state** (a
77	  title match against what's declared at HEAD, a computed membership test) — reconsider once the
78	  derivation's own inputs can mutate while the classified object stays open. A "standing vs
79	  ad-hoc" task classification computed live from whether an issue's title matched a task declared
80	  at HEAD silently reinterpreted an open issue's own history the moment that task's frequency or
81	  name changed underneath it. An explicit marker stamped once at creation and never revisited
82	  doesn't have that failure mode — the general preference for a structural classifier over a
83	  hand-set field holds only for state that isn't itself still in flight (#1120).
84	
85	- **Scheduling the removal of a temporary compatibility tolerance** (an old-format reader, a
86	  legacy-field fallback) — gate the removal on a converge-cycle-confirmable precondition ("no
87	  member still stamps the legacy format"), never a calendar date alone. Retiring the tolerance
88	  while a member is still on the old format doesn't just leave that member behind: the value it
89	  stamps starts reading as "no version installed" to the now-stricter reader, which re-applies
90	  every migration record in the corpus (#1106).
91	
92	## Working with the owner and the session's tools
93	
94	- **Answering "why did it fail?"** — lead with the throwing call site: `file:line`, the
95	  function, and which side enforced it. A correct narrative that never names the line reads as
96	  unanswered.
97	
98	- **Reaching for `AskUserQuestion`** — it blocks for minutes (~170s median), so spend it only
99	  on a fork you cannot take back. Anything answerable from the instruction, the tree, or a
100	  reversible default: answer it, act, and say what you assumed. Never re-post a question that was
101	  declined — take its recommended default, or open the question up.
102	
103	- **Being asked to generalise something, or to review it** — land the conversions or action
104	  points it unlocks in the same change. A capability ships with the caller that exercises it; an
105	  analysis ships with the first of its recommendations applied.
106	
107	- **Calling anything on `Claude_Code_Remote`** — one call per intent, ever. Each costs
108	  minutes, and a call that returns nothing has *not* failed — the retry has run to 81% of a
109	  session's tool wall-clock. For "is it green yet" read the check status directly; to read a
110	  public sibling repo, `git clone --depth 1` (~2s), since `add_repo` attaches nothing the git
111	  proxy doesn't already serve.
112	
113	- **Waiting for something to happen** — the guard must name the condition awaited (a run's
114	  status, a file's arrival, a deadline), with no trailing padded `sleep`. A guard you wouldn't
115	  write as the *whole* test means you are sleeping and calling it polling. **Exception: GitHub
116	  CI/PR check status is not this repo's case for `Monitor` or a `curl`/shell poll loop** — this
117	  sandbox proxy-blocks `api.github.com`, so both silently report "still running" until they time
118	  out (measured ~26 minutes lost across two PRs waiting past an already-green check, #880). Read
119	  the head sha's check runs with the GitHub MCP tool instead. Poll it on a rolling backoff, or
120	  not at all when a background watcher already reports that signal.
121	
122	- **Writing a step a human must do by hand into an issue** — when asking for a manual action,
123	  make absolutely sure it is needed: a checklist whose items are mostly no-ops teaches the reader
124	  to skim it, exactly what the checklist exists to prevent. Make the breadcrumb trail a
125	  hyperlink, to the deepest existing settings URL — a link keeps working or redirects where a
126	  written-out trail goes stale the moment GitHub reorganizes the page (#952, owner-authored).
127	
128	- **Replying to an owner comment that raises more than one claim** — answer **every** claim in
129	  that first reply, including the one you intend to push back on. A claim left silently
130	  unaddressed, even when the rest of the reply is right, just makes the owner re-raise it later
131	  (#864: a placement objection went unanswered for 55 minutes before the owner repeated it).
132	
133	- **Repeating a design doc's stated architectural rationale** — verify each of its claimed
134	  grounds against the current code (declared secrets, executor permissions) before reciting it
135	  again, especially once a direct challenge has already found it wrong once. The same overstated
136	  "a task structurally cannot hold this permission" argument was corrected twice in one session —
137	  once for a GitHub Pages deploy, again minutes later for a chrome-extension release — because
138	  code-work already runs inside the executor's own Action job with the permissions in question
139	  (#1069).
140	
141	- **An owner reversing a standing decision** — the fix is not answering the question that
142	  prompted it, it is finding and purging every place in the repo (docs, comments, code defaults)
143	  that still states the old decision, and recording the new one where a future session reads it
144	  before ever asserting the stale version again. One reversal (turning local scheduling on,
145	  moving `canon-curation`) had to be repeated five times before a session treated it as a
146	  durable-artifact problem rather than a one-off answer (#364).
147	
148	- **Firing `AskUserQuestion` on a vague, destructive-sounding instruction** ("remove the entire
149	  mechanism," "get rid of the whole thing") — scope the question to pin down the boundary of the
150	  vague noun itself, not just the downstream consequences of one reading of it. A question that
151	  asked only what happens to the one dependent check, while silently assuming "entire mechanism"
152	  meant the whole engine surface, let 15 minutes of deletion, test-authoring and PR/issue
153	  bookkeeping land before the owner caught it nine minutes later and all of it was discarded with
154	  a hard reset (#1114).
155	
156	## Authoring packs, prose and checks
157	
158	- **Writing a paragraph that explains how a mechanism works** — not into a pack's `RULES.md`,
159	  which every session in every declaring repo pays for. Behaviour belongs in the module header and
160	  the pack `README.md`; the test is whether an agent could act differently for having read it.
161	
162	- **Having a deferred direction, blocked proposal or status to record** — put it in `docs/`
163	  and point at it from the issue or PR, not from a pack file: `docs/` is outside the vendor set.
164	
165	- **Naming a new canon pack** — kebab-case, named for the surface it serves rather than the
166	  first feature you are building for it. A pack whose subject is a **Claudinite feature itself**,
167	  rather than a technology or a way of working, carries the `claudinite-` prefix
168	  (`claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-growth`, `claudinite-dashboard`) — owner, 2026-08-18.
169	  The directory name is the pack's public id, spelled in
170	  every member's declaration, so another casing costs a fleet-wide rename. `claudinite-growth`
171	  is grandfathered. (convertible → prose-to-checks)
172	
173	- **Starting a new Claudinite-facing capability** (a tool, a dashboard, anything meant to reach
174	  more than the current repo) — decide **which distribution model it is** before writing the
175	  first file: a member-local tool, always-on engine code, or an opt-in pack with its own
176	  adoption/scaffolding. Nothing prompts this choice on its own, and getting it wrong costs a full
177	  move-and-rewrite cycle per correction — one session paid it three times in a row before landing
178	  on "opt-in pack" (#934).
179	
180	- **Looking for a skill and not finding it in `.claude/skills/`** — read
181	  `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree. Mounting filters on the *literal*
182	  declaration and the home doesn't declare `git-github`, so an unmounted skill says nothing about
183	  whether its procedure applies.
184	
185	- **Adding or changing a check** — update the pack's catalog row, and re-run the suite against
186	  current `main` before merging: a whole-tree aggregate is judged post-merge, so a branch's own green
187	  never covers it. Never transcribe a corpus-wide total into a doc — `packs/README.md` states how to
188	  count checks and rules instead of quoting a number, so every pack change no longer edits it.
189	  (portable → `merge-to-main`)
190	
191	- **Writing a check's `fix` text** — name only remedies that match the enforced severity;
192	  sessions follow the words, not the `severity` field. An advisory finding's remedies are act on
193	  it or leave it, never a config-acceptance escape.
194	
195	- **Declaring a check, or adding a key to the vocabulary** — name the key so the declaration
196	  reads alone to someone who hasn't read the design doc (`scanFiles`, `matchLines`,
197	  `relevantWhen`): if it needs a comment to be read, it needs a better name. Declarations live in
198	  `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`, which cannot hold one, and borrow nothing from prose — no
199	  `description`, no `doc`; the line the agent reads is `failureMessage`.
200	
201	- **Writing a check that reads the session transcript** — screen the harness's own **plain-text**
202	  pseudo-turns, not only the tag-wrapped ones. `humanText` in
203	  `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs` drops a user entry that starts with `<`, which
204	  lets a bracketed marker straight through: `comment-classification` blocked a session on
205	  `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]` as "the owner's latest comment". A conversation rule
206	  fires at the Stop hook, where a false positive spends a whole cycle on something no edit can
207	  clear — so its fixture carries an interruption marker beside a real owner turn.
208	
209	- **A doc reached only by following a link out of `RULES.md` or a check's `doc:`/`More:` line** —
210	  if it is a how-to wanted at authoring time rather than prose every session should carry, convert
211	  it into a skill (frontmatter + description) invocable by description, not a doc chained through
212	  links nobody follows cold (#975).
213	
214	- **A check declaration's `doc:` field** — nothing ever opens it; it only renders into a finding's
215	  `More:` line when the check actually fires. A stale pointer left by a file move can sit broken
216	  indefinitely with nothing to catch it — grep for and re-verify every `doc:` field by hand
217	  whenever you move or rename the file it points at (#975).
218	
219	- **A check built to catch a thing being missing or misnamed** — don't gate the check's own
220	  relevance on the single signal it exists to validate. Gating solely on "does the orchestrating
221	  file still have the expected name" makes the exact failure the check exists to catch (a rename)
222	  also the thing that silences the check — the run that should say "rename it back" never fires.
223	  Use two independent signals, either sufficient, so at least one survives when the other is the
224	  thing that broke (#1060).
225	
226	- **Deciding whether an enforced check still earns its keep** — measure its actual blocking-firing
227	  rate against what it buys, not vibes. A check whose firings are dominated by cases where the
228	  agent had already done the right thing, and the check only wants the exact tokens for it, is a
229	  demotion candidate (check → prose-only), justified by the firing-frequency data itself:
230	  `comment-classification` fired 204 times in 31 days, 21% of all blocking findings, each one a
231	  blocked Stop-hook turn spent re-emitting a line the session had already been told to emit
232	  (#1118).
233	
234	- **A documented multi-step procedure the agent re-derives interactively every time it runs** —
235	  that pattern, not the doc's polish, is the signal to mechanize it into a script the agent runs
236	  once. A nine-part prose bootstrap doc cost ~90 exploratory tool calls and ~11 minutes per
237	  adoption for work that runs in seconds once scripted. Part of that cost was sequencing, not
238	  exploration: the tracking issue was created only after the first commit had already failed the
239	  issue-reference check, costing a full amend/force-push/CI cycle — create the artifact a check
240	  will demand *before* the action it gates, not after (#1132).
241	
242	## The engine, the mount and what reaches members
243	
244	- **Writing a path, regex or command against the mount** — write the two-root form: the
245	  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix optional in a pattern, and a probe for
246	  `.claudinite/shared/` falling back to the repo root. The home runs the same code from the repo
247	  root, so a mount-shaped path works fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — where it
248	  surfaces last.
249	
250	- **Adding a module under `packs/`** — keep it import-light, and start work after evaluation
251	  completes (`check(…).catch(…)`), never in a top-level `await`. Discovery imports every
252	  `pack.mjs` and `checks.mjs` before activation is consulted, so a module that is also a CLI entry
253	  point is re-imported mid-evaluation and Node exits 13 having run nothing.
254	  `pack-discovery-entry-await` enforces the await half only.
255	
256	- **Tightening a contract that member-owned files must satisfy** — first ask what carries it
257	  across the fleet. Vendoring refreshes `.claudinite/shared/` only and a migration record moves
258	  paths, not schemas — so if the answer is "nothing", accept the legacy shape in
259	  `normalizeManifest` until a carrier exists. Never let a stale declaration degrade to *fewer
260	  checks running* rather than a failure.
261	
262	- **Renaming a pack whose config a member writes into their own repo** — the rename map fixes
263	  code-side id resolution, but it cannot rewrite a member's own already-committed config, which
264	  converges on its own separate schedule or never. A reader consuming that config keeps resolving
265	  both the new key and every legacy spelling explicitly and permanently: rewriting the write side
266	  to the new name (the fix for the fleet's own persisted data) only helps where the engine itself
267	  owns the write, not data a member wrote into their own repo (#1081).
268	
269	- **Checking whether an actor may trigger a privileged automated action off a GitHub issue/PR
270	  payload** — read the actor's permission from the collaborators-permission API
271	  (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`), never the payload's `author_association`:
272	  `MEMBER` covers any org member regardless of repo permission, and `COLLABORATOR` includes
273	  read-only collaborators — both broader than push access (#1067).
274	
275	- **Extending what a copied stub reads** — make the new config key optional, fail the run when
276	  it is declared-but-unset, and let declaring it trigger a staleness check (`build_vars` /
277	  `release-workflows` is the shape). Stubs are copied into a member's `.github/` once and never
278	  re-copied, so a new key is silently dead in every repo holding the old copy.
279	
280	- **Writing a migration record that needs engine behaviour newer than itself** — have
281	  `appliesTo` probe the member's own mount for that capability, by content rather than version,
282	  and stay inert until it reads back; an unreadable mount must read as "not capable". The record
283	  comes from a fresh canon clone but the worker executing it is the member's vendored one, so
284	  otherwise the converge fails, the mount never advances, and the fix can never arrive.
285	
286	- **Changing an export in `updates/*`** — empty it, never remove it. Fielded workers are stale
287	  callers of instantly-current flow modules, so a removal wedges every member permanently on its
288	  next run. Keep it callable, say at its definition that this is why, and pin the surface with a
289	  test carrying an expiry — the canary rehearsal cannot catch this class, since it drives the
290	  worker this ref ships. Retire it by reading the field: the condition is that no member's
291	  *vendored* worker calls it.
292	
293	- **Renaming or deleting an `engine/` module a `packs/` file imports** — leave a shim at the old
294	  path re-exporting what it named, for the same reason and by the same rule as `updates/*` above:
295	  the engine lane and the pack lane deliver in separate PRs on separate cycles, and pack delivery is
296	  version-gated per pack, so every member spends a window holding the NEW engine beside an OLD pack.
297	  The failure is worse than a broken task — a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test,
298	  the converge then refuses to land AT ALL, and the member cannot receive the pack version that
299	  would have fixed it (#1004: a green run, an unmoved stamp, and a `needs-human` PR). Ask which
300	  symbols are fielded by walking the TRUNK's pack history, never `--all` — an import that only ever
301	  existed on an unmerged branch is not fielded, and scanning every ref fires on whatever is in
302	  flight.
303	
304	- **Changing a vendored stub** — edit the canon's own `.github/workflows/` copy in the same
305	  commit and diff the two whole files. The canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly
306	  until it is a permission denial in production.
307	
308	- **Excluding files from the vendor set by pattern** — whitelist any operational file that
309	  matches by path, and pin it with a test against the real canon tree, not only a fixture. The
310	  nightly refresh re-runs the computation from canon HEAD, so a bug there is the one canon
311	  regression that is not self-healing. Assert that the **whole containing directory** vendors,
312	  not just the one file that broke — a test re-asserting only the known-missing file needs a
313	  fresh edit for the next file added there; one that walks the real directory doesn't (#907).
314	
315	- **Retiring or reshaping a protocol the engine exposes** (a dispatch input, a stub's declared
316	  interface) — sweep for callers **outside this repo**, not just what greps locally. `FORCE_TASKS`'s
317	  replacement broke Shepherd's only caller because the migration enumerated this repo's own
318	  callers and missed the cross-repo one (#929); two independently-maintained stub copies at the
319	  same path declaring different input names is the same failure from the other side (#801, #907)
320	  — the two spellings *are* the protocol, and they live in different trees.
321	
322	- **Branching on the result of an API write in fleet machinery** — read its status, not just
323	  the body: a body-only destructure turns a 403 into a plausible object and the run still logs
324	  `ok`. Judge the fleet by members' stamps, never by run conclusions — the stamp is the only
325	  artifact that moves when delivery actually worked.
326	
327	- **A single timeout bound covering two different waits** ("has this even started" vs. "is
328	  something already running about to finish") reintroduces the bug a prior fix closed, on
329	  whichever side crosses the shorter phase's real need. Split the bound to match what each phase
330	  is actually waiting on, sized from that work's own declared budget rather than a round number —
331	  and once a bound is hit, the give-up message must never read as a verdict on the work: "no
332	  successful run yet" is a statement about the clock, not about the runs, and collapsing the two
333	  sent a reader chasing a wrong repository-settings diagnosis for CI that was simply still running
334	  (#1027).
335	
336	- **Writing generated content into a size-capped GitHub API field** (an issue or PR body) —
337	  budget it explicitly, in two tiers: an always-complete compact summary plus best-effort detail
338	  rationed to a byte budget with an explicit omitted-count, never a single unbounded write that
339	  can 422 outright at the ~64KB cap. `growth-dedup`'s brief rendered 350KB against that limit and
340	  would have failed the run at its first step.
341	
342	- **Writing a generated title whose naive content scales with a variable-length list** (a PR
343	  title, a notification headline) — collapse the list to a count and keep the per-item detail in
344	  the body. A title is a summary surface, not a second body, and grows unreadable exactly where a
345	  long list makes every character compete for space (#1048).
346	
347	- **Preflighting a required grant or permission** — a probe is only as good as the environment it
348	  runs against; where the failure is conditional (a scope that 403s only under a specific
349	  condition, e.g. a private repo), a probe run where that condition isn't met reports a
350	  false-positive pass. Prefer attributing a real observed 403 to the permission that would fix it
351	  over guessing from an unrepresentative probe (#1052).
352	
353	- **Introducing a finer-grained classification of an existing catch-all state** — default
354	  whatever an older or unaware writer produces (or a future writer's not-yet-known category) to
355	  the most conservative member of the new set, not the most lenient. An unlabelled park now reads
356	  as the blocking `failure` lane rather than a soft one, so a writer that predates the split fails
357	  safe instead of silently landing in a lane nobody watches (#1051).
358	
359	- **Adding a fleet task** — fail loudly on a Context target it cannot reach rather than
360	  proceeding on a partial list, and treat a member as un-adopted until the routine's repo scope
361	  names it. The target list is enumerated over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` while the grant is hand-typed
362	  UI config no Action can read; the drift *completes*, filing a report that reads as a full sweep.
363	
364	- **Spawning a child process from a worker** — pass an explicit `cwd`, resolved to a root that
365	  cannot vanish (`--root`, then `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, then `cwd`). The converge deletes the tree
366	  its own code-work runs inside, so children die at `process.cwd()` before doing anything. Keep
367	  "could not run" distinguishable from "had nothing to run": a crash sharing a benign outcome code
368	  is unobservable.
369	
370	- **Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land** — `unstable` beside a green sweep
371	  is a parked `action_required` run, not a missing repo setting. Read the member's raw
372	  `.claudinite-checks.json` and the head sha's `pull_request` runs; propose a platform-settings
373	  change only as a conclusion, never as a diagnosis.
374	
375	- **Judging whether a member is fresh** — read its `ref` (or `engineVersion` /
376	  `packVersions`), never `claudinite.updated` alone: a held stamp pins `updated` behind a pending
377	  note, so a mount converging hourly can look a week stale.
378	
379	- **Reading a uniform signal across every fleet member right after a shared mechanism changes**
380	  — a rate-limited, unauthenticated `api.github.com` probe can return a clean-looking uniform
381	  negative across every target, and a uniform stamp/ref shared by the whole fleet can mean "not
382	  yet past its nightly anchor" rather than "frozen." Check for a rate-limit signal explicitly
383	  before trusting a uniform empty sweep, and check timing — has each member's own convergence
384	  window actually passed — before generalizing one member's confirmed fault to the fleet. Never
385	  reuse a signal already known unreliable to corroborate a different theory (#801, #939: a "the
386	  entire fleet is frozen" claim stood uncorrected for ~10 hours).
387	
388	- **Retiring or migrating a dispatch/config parameter channel** — a parameter that stops being
389	  read must fail loudly, never silently default. A dropped safety knob (e.g. `DRY_RUN`) defaults
390	  to the operation's *most dangerous* mode — live, unscoped — not a safe one; audit that a
391	  parameter's producer and consumer still agree after every interface migration (#974,
392	  owner-authored).
393	
394	- **Relying on a push to trigger further Actions workflows** — a push authored with the default
395	  `GITHUB_TOKEN` (which every converge and auto-merge in this repo's own machinery uses) fires no
396	  `on: push` workflow; only a push carrying a real user or app credential cascades. A dashboard
397	  stuck showing a stale "hasn't converged" banner traced back to exactly this: the deploy
398	  workflow's trigger never fired for the pushes that actually moved a mount (#1094). The same
399	  platform fact is why `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push into — it lands
400	  only through a PR a human merges — so a renamed or removed entry point that a workflow file
401	  references by literal path needs a shim held open until every consumer's own copy has moved, by
402	  the same rule as an `engine/` module a `packs/` file imports (#1108).
403	
404	- **A script written for one execution context silently breaking in another** — audit every
405	  script's environment assumptions (a real `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `gh`/`curl` reachability) whenever the
406	  execution context of its caller changes, not just at the one call site that surfaced the break.
407	  A script written when the queue ran as an Actions job (a real token, shell GitHub access) 401'd
408	  once the same work started running inside an agent session (MCP-only, a proxy-scoped token, no
409	  `gh`) — and per the owner, every other script built against the old assumption fails identically
410	  in the new context, not just the one that broke first (#1133).
411	
412	- **Finding a check that watches only one of two structurally-identical surfaces** — widen it to
413	  the sibling in the same change rather than filing it separately. A check exercising the
414	  scheduler's own vendored stub had never been extended to the executor's stub, which is just as
415	  much a fleet-wide vendored surface and just as capable of drifting unnoticed (#1138).
416	
417	- **Picking a compact date-encoded identifier** (a version stamp, a compact timestamp) — check
418	  the encoding's own rollover boundary years ahead, not just today's decode correctness: anchoring
419	  a year on its last digit wraps to 0 in 2030 and sorts a decade of releases underneath every 2029
420	  one, so the anchor point matters (`year - 2020`, not `year % 10`). And keep the identifier
421	  string-typed everywhere it travels — `'60820.10'` and `'60820.1'` are different versions and the
422	  same float, so nothing in the corpus may parse one as a number (#1105).
423	
424	- **Designing text that instructs a model to echo an exact string** (a session-start directive, a
425	  generated title) — don't reference the payload anaphorically from later text ("that line," "the
426	  above"); state the instruction first, have it disclaim itself as instruction-not-payload, and
427	  put the literal string once, last, introduced by the instruction's own colon. Recency is what an
428	  LLM actually resolves ambiguous reference against: putting the directive *after* the payload
429	  line made "that line" read as the directive sentence itself, and a session opened two replies in
430	  a row reciting the instruction verbatim instead of the summary (#1126).
431	
432	## Scheduled tasks
433	
434	- **Choosing a task's cadence** — take it from how often the signal actually moves. A
435	  precondition reading `sharedMount` fires nearly every night and spends an opus session on it;
436	  where the work isn't latency-sensitive, daily buys noise, not freshness, and a weekly run still
437	  sees all 7 days because a task's signal window is its OWN period plus an hour of slack.
438	
439	- **After any scheduler-mechanism flip** (how forced/manual work is dispatched, how a
440	  precondition is evaluated) — re-audit every task whose precondition assumed the old mechanism.
441	  A stale `run: false` that was previously "consulted by nothing" becomes a live self-closing
442	  landmine under the new mechanism — the third instance of this exact class in this repo (#929,
443	  #921, #971); grep for `frequency: 'manual'` plus its precondition text, not just the flipped
444	  mechanism's own callers.
445	
446	- **Writing a task's precondition** — gate on the objects' own movement in the window (a
447	  `touched` list, a tip-commit date the collector actually carries), never on standing state,
448	  which is true forever once true. A signal true most days — a substantive `main` move — may
449	  only *widen* an already-triggered run. The gate is not the scope: where a verdict is relative to
450	  the rest of the set, newness gates and the full set stays the scope. (portable →
451	  `claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md`)
452	
453	- **Writing a task whose output is a regenerated file** — land it through
454	  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` and read its prior state from the fetched base, not
455	  local HEAD. One executor run drains several items from one checkout, so a worker that checks out
456	  a branch or leaves an index behind hands the next item a tree it did not expect.
457	  (`basics/baselining` is the deliberate exception.)
458	
459	- **Wanting to exercise a task Action-side** — dispatch the scheduler workflow with its `wake`
460	  input naming the task, which clears the standing item's wait and puts it back in the queue; the
461	  post-scheduler run drain then picks it up in the same run. The precondition is still evaluated at pickup,
462	  so a wake that finds no work SAYS so on the item — a forced run that does nothing is a verdict,
463	  not a failure. (Under the retired slot scheduler this did not work at all: dueness was stateless,
464	  so an off-window `workflow_dispatch` printed `- no tasks due` and looked exactly like a healthy
465	  run.)
466	
467	- **Converging an unattended run** — do the final label/comment/close sequence as the run's very
468	  next action once the outcome is known, not deferred to a checklist recalled from memory at the
469	  end of a long session, when context is fullest and the remaining work looks like formality.
470	  Two runs closed `outcome:done` while their own PR sat open needing a human, and one skipped the
471	  outcome label and the exec record entirely (#939, #892) — five days of green-looking runs on
472	  one of them. `outcome:done` means nothing is left for anyone to act on; never close it while a
473	  PR, branch, or open question from this run is still live.
474	
475	- **Decomposing a pipeline into chained tasks** — chain stages by preconditions that each
476	  re-derive the world's actual state, never by parameters or Context passed forward. A run
477	  interrupted mid-pipeline then self-heals on the next pick instead of needing `on_interrupt`
478	  handling at every stage, and `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` narrows to the one stage whose side
479	  effect is genuinely non-idempotent (#1073).
480	
481	- **Passing a diagnostic verdict out of a subprocess that may be killed at its own timeout
482	  ceiling** — write it to the live output stream (stdout/stderr), never to a file meant to be
483	  written at exit: already-printed output survives a `SIGKILL`, a file written on the way out is
484	  never written at all if the kill lands first (#1051).
485	
486	- **Writing a stateless reconciliation or repair rule over a live, mutating collection** (a
487	  janitor sweep, a stale-item rule) — distinguish rules gated on a *clock* (elapsed time, safe
488	  against snapshot staleness) from rules gated on *current state* (need a fresh, targeted read of
489	  the specific item immediately before acting, never the snapshot that triggered the sweep). An
490	  item that settled between the sweep's read and its write is otherwise indistinguishable from a
491	  genuinely torn state machine: a claim-to-close window that had shrunk to ~4 seconds let a janitor
492	  rule stamp `task:done` and `needs-human` on an issue that had already succeeded (#1101, fixed in
493	  #1108).
494	
495	- **Solving a "must act again later" or "must verify eventually" problem** — check whether an
496	  existing generic lane already gives you everything before building new standing machinery for
497	  it. A first cut added a whole new daily task, keyed on a title-prefix scan, to handle deferred
498	  production-verification; the owner pointed at the deferred-request queue's existing
499	  `Blocked-by`/`Not-before` lane, which already carried it end to end, and the bespoke task — a
500	  second queue standing beside the first — came back out (#1092).
501	
502	## Proving a change
503	
504	- **Testing a change to a task's triggering** — drive the real `planSchedulerRun` from a clock at which
505	  the task's anchor has NOT come. Instantiation is decided before any precondition runs, so a test
506	  that starts from an item already in the queue proves only "works once instantiated" and says
507	  nothing about whether the occurrence is ever created.
508	
509	- **Testing a fail-soft step** — assert the positive effect (the output IS emitted), never
510	  `status === 0`, which fail-soft makes meaningless. The engine is vendored verbatim, so one such
511	  regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet.
512	
513	- **Writing a check that selects inputs by path pattern** — assert over the real tree that its
514	  scope is non-empty; a pattern left behind by a layout change matches nothing, reads as live and
515	  catches nothing, and fixtures spelling the same dead layout keep proving the matching. Likewise
516	  grep the tree for any directory you name in a finding, a remedy or a doc pointer before shipping
517	  it.
518	
519	- **Testing a helper reapplied across a hand-off, a re-queue or a retry** — call it twice and
520	  assert no duplication. A suite of single-call tests stays green while the multi-call case
521	  corrupts state. When the mechanism arbitrates by identity (a claim, a lock), the second call
522	  must come from a **different actor** — a single actor retrying its own stale claim can't expose
523	  an identity-masked race, which is exactly what hid F18 until two distinct executors raced (#925).
524	
525	- **Building or extending a simulator for a stateful engine mechanism** — model what the real
526	  engine's code actually *writes* (the artifact), never the rule's stated *intent*. A sim that
527	  advances state on every transition matching the rule's description, rather than only where the
528	  real engine leaves a mark, is correct by construction and blind to exactly the silent paths
529	  where the two diverge — which is where the bug lived (an episode-boundary livelock, #925).
530	
531	- **Asserting a mid-run invariant in a simulator or test** — capture it at the exact moment the
532	  state holds, not after the run continues past it. A check re-queued before an item had ever left
533	  a state asserted over an item that never actually failed; by the end of the run normal
534	  convergence had already cleared the evidence the assertion meant to catch (#1054).
535	
536	- **A test that derives its answer by walking git history** (which imports are still fielded, from
537	  trunk) — guard explicitly against a shallow clone and fail loudly rather than silently evaluate
538	  over whatever partial history happens to be present. A shallow checkout would otherwise let the
539	  test pass vacuously exactly when the real answer needs history it doesn't have (#1013).
540	
541	- **Restoring source after a deliberate see-it-fail mutation** — `git checkout -- <file>` (or
542	  `git stash`) at the moment of mutating, never a `.bak` copy taken earlier: a `.bak` predates
543	  whatever else you edited in between, and restoring from it silently destroys that work (#922).
544	  `git checkout --` restores from the index, so it destroys *uncommitted* work in the same file
545	  just as thoroughly. Commit or stage the real edit **before** mutating anything to see it fail,
546	  and only mutate a file whose current state you are ready to throw away (#1010).
547	
548	- **Running the test suite** — `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. There is no test
549	  script, and every hand-written glob under-runs it silently: `node --test <dir>` doesn't recurse,
550	  and bash `**` without `globstar` reached 37 of 65 files. `ci.yml`'s array is not authoritative
551	  either. Redirect one run to a file and grep that file for whatever slice you need next — never
552	  re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice the same unchanged output (five reruns cost 4.5 minutes for
553	  five different greps, #930, #931).
554	
555	- **Iterating on a sweep across many files** — while iterating, run only the test files the edit
556	  touches plus `check_the_work`; spend the whole suite and `check_the_world` once, at the end,
557	  before the commit. Both are whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file of a
558	  sweep, and re-running them per edit is what the session actually costs: of one night's tool
559	  wall-clock, the session that landed #993 spent 18 full-suite runs (18 min) and 22 world sweeps
560	  (7 min) out of 26 min, #941's spent 22 (22 min) and 27 (12 min) out of 33 min, and #992's 7 and
561	  8 out of 14 min.
562	
563	- **Surveying whether something exists in the tree** — a code-search hit is evidence; a
564	  code-search miss is not. Survey by reading each file.
565	
566	- **Documenting or relying on a named knob** (a declaration field, an env var, a config key, a
567	  counter series) — the corpus naming it is not evidence it exists: grep for the code that
568	  **reads** it and the code that **writes** it first. One window turned up all three misses.
569	  Designed and never built, documented as live: `CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL`, beside `exclusive`
570	  which had retired with its mechanism (#975). A writer with no reader left: `session_scope`, with
571	  nothing saying so (#993). And a reader with no writer left: the usage fold's `tasks` census,
572	  whose parser outlived the log lines it read, so the rows keep counting plausibly until the
573	  Actions retention window ages out and then count nothing (#994). That last shape is the one to
574	  design against — deleting a writer is the same change as marking its series historical, never
575	  something to notice later when the numbers reach zero.
576	
577	- **Writing check-the-work** — make sure you validate it fails: create the conditions that fail
578	  the check and see it go red (#966, #970).
579	
580	- **Renaming an entity** — sweep for references in code and comments, don't change historical
581	  records, and re-render generated files rather than editing them by hand (#957).
582	
583	- **Renaming a word that is also stored data** (a counter key, a wire word, a label) — the sweep
584	  is not finished at the code. A persisted aggregate holds rows keyed by the old spelling, so the
585	  **decode** side must rename them too, or the next encode writes those historical counts as
586	  `null` — silently, and only for the old rows. And on a *second* rename of one name, map every
587	  legacy spelling **straight to today's** rather than chaining one normalization onto the last, so
588	  a declaration written for the oldest vocabulary still normalizes in a single pass (#1013).
589	
590	- **Writing a "this period is covered" marker in an at-least-once or idempotent pipeline** (a
591	  watermark row, a dedup stamp) — write it strictly after the durable effect it is guarding, and
592	  never let it stand in as proof the effect happened. Modeling a decision row as sufficient cover
593	  for its period ate a real occurrence whenever the item the row promised had failed to actually
594	  get created: a write failure was silently read as "already handled," the exact inversion of the
595	  system's own fail-open policy. Caught by the simulator before any engine code shipped; the fix
596	  scopes the marker to the *declined* case only — a go verdict's coverage is judged by the item it
597	  actually created, never by the row (#1123).
598	
599	## Editing, branching and merging here
600	
601	- **Making a throwaway probe commit on a scratch branch to see a check fail** — `git commit -am`
602	  stages *every* modified file, not just the probe's own change; a subsequent `git branch -D` of
603	  that scratch branch discards any real in-progress edit it swept up along with the probe. Stash
604	  or otherwise isolate real pending edits first (#939).
605	
606	- **Editing a repo's JSON config** — patch it as anchored text; never re-serialize. A
607	  round-trip rewrites what it wasn't asked to (`ensure_ascii` escapes, indent, key order, trailing
608	  newline) while nothing fails and tests stay green. (portable → `repo-text-sweeps`) **Exception:**
609	  when the target can sit inside a nested array within an entry object (e.g. a pack's own
610	  `via`/`config` array nested inside its `{"id": …}` entry), an anchored regex cannot cross the
611	  nested closing bracket, so every element after it goes silently unreached — and a fixture built
612	  without that nesting proves nothing, since it spells the same gap the pattern has. Parse and
613	  rewrite structurally there instead, preserving key order/config/`via`/answers by hand (#1042).
614	
615	- **Returning to a branch that waited** — after `git fetch`, re-verify the *premise*, unasked:
616	  read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and say whether the problem is
617	  still there and what survives. This repo auto-merges its own PRs on top of migrations that
618	  retire whole directories, so a branch can rebase cleanly, stay green, and no longer be the
619	  change to make.
620	
621	- **Re-verifying a branch against a `main` that has moved** — `git rebase origin/main`, never
622	  `git merge origin/main`. A merge commit trips the blocking squash-merge-history check and costs
623	  a full rebase, a discarded CI run, and a fresh wait — paid twice in one evening on #880.
624	
625	- **After a PR lands by squash-merge** — `git remote prune origin` before touching that branch
626	  again. GitHub deletes the head ref on squash-merge here, so a stale local tracking ref makes git
627	  count the pre-squash commits as unpushed: the next push is rejected and the stop hook reports
628	  phantom local work (#922).
629	
630	- **Re-applying your edit onto a moved `main`** — re-read the fetched file, apply the same
631	  anchored edit, and confirm the stat shows insertions only. A pack's `RULES.md` is append-only
632	  and written several times a day, so restoring a whole-file copy deletes those lessons and
633	  nothing goes red.
634	
635	- **Syncing local `main`** — `git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`,
636	  unconditionally. The clones are shallow, so `git pull` finds no common ancestor and reports the
637	  stale local ref as carrying unique commits; nothing of value is ever on this repo's local
638	  `main`. (portable → `git-github`)
639	
640	- **Merging in a session that also has a consumer repo in its sources** — resolve the merge
641	  skill by *target repo*, not by which skill matched first. The consumer's skill wins on name and
642	  is followed to the letter, silently skipping the canon-only steps — repeatedly the post-merge
643	  conversation capture (`node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), which is
644	  part of the merge, not an optional epilogue.
645	
646	- **Having work that completes or corrects an open PR** — put it on that PR's branch. A
647	  dispatch prompt's designated branch routes work, not review; splitting gives the owner two gates
648	  for one decision and invites approving half.
649	
650	- **Wanting to combine two PRs** — update the one you're keeping and close the other. Never
651	  push one's branch onto the other's base: GitHub marks a PR merged as soon as its head is
652	  reachable from its base, and a later `state: closed` is a no-op. Check the API's `merged` field
653	  before reporting.
654	
655	- **Being asked "should no X decide this?"** — it questions whether the decision exists at
656	  all; never answer it by relocating the knob one rung out. Ask who would ever set it differently
657	  and why that can't be read off the structure — a single structural answer means delete the
658	  field and document the exception where it lives.
659	
660	- **Facing a retry across a call whose outcome you cannot observe** — check whether declining
661	  to retry removes the uncertainty before building dedup or arbitration machinery to manage it. A
662	  timeout is exactly the case where you cannot know the first call did nothing.
663
